question: With a shared observation interface and objective, can a bounded hazard-aware DQN learn useful adjustments, and does it add value beyond snapshot replanning?

observation.contract: Position one-hot, current full-map FER/0.012, elapsed control steps/128, cumulative personal FED. Map and legal moves common to all policies. No scenario ID, hazardous side/center, future onset or future FER in policy input. This does not guarantee full Markov observability.

ablation: Both arms have the same 50-input architecture, initial parameters per seed, clock, cumulative FED, action mask, objective and step/update budgets. Blind arm zeroes only FER indices 24:48 in its effective observation; own exposure can still indirectly reveal hazards.

training.reward: r=-20*(step_FED+0.00125), with extra -40 if the 128-step task horizon ends without exit. No revisit penalty or exit bonus. Within successful episodes undiscounted return=-20*J. Finite task horizon and terminal failure are explicit; stopping the 40000-step training budget mid-episode does not change task terminal flags.
training.legal_action_mask: Apply during random exploration, greedy action selection and TD target maximization. No hazard hard mask.
training.episode_schedule: Repeated shuffled complete blocks of all 24 training scenarios, seeded per training seed; same episode scenario schedule for paired arms, although trajectory lengths differ. Record actual visitation.
training.checkpoints: Final weights only; no performance-based checkpoint/seed selection, no evaluation until all six models are locked.

development_bank.visibility: Eight previously used relative probe patterns; descriptive development results only, no retuning in this round.

confirmation_bank.visibility: 24 new deterministic parameter combinations frozen before training; not the old sealed 48 final scenarios. Only scored after all model hashes are locked.

primary: First compare reached exit; among successful paired cases report FED, time and J=FED+0.00125*steps. Never silently drop failures or rank a failure by its partial exposure. Descriptive seed and scenario summaries; no independent-fire or significance claim.

frozen_decision_rules.observation_signal_supported: On confirmation, all full models reach every exit and paired full mean J is lower than paired blind mean J for each of the three training seeds. If blind failures occur, report them explicitly and compare successful common cases separately.
frozen_decision_rules.practical_RL_added_value: All full models reach every confirmation exit and each has mean J at least 5% below the shared-observation snapshot_replan mean, with no higher mean FED and mean time no more than 5% above planner. Otherwise do not claim extra RL value.
frozen_decision_rules.near_planner: If all full models succeed and all have mean J no more than 5% above planner, describe approximate usability only; this is not superiority.
frozen_decision_rules.stop: One 240000-transition training round, 288 evaluation episodes, no post-result budget increase or hyperparameter search. Close with results even if criteria fail.

scope: New engineering objective and observed-hazard DQN extension, not author SafeStep code/numeric reproduction. Synthetic fixed-layout mechanism evidence, not human or real-fire validation. No LLM/PPO or old sealed-bank access.
